$comment: cuesea Brand & Identity System v3.2 (August 2026). CANONICAL. Every app's brand.css is generated from this file by `npm run brand:sync` - do not hand-edit the generated copies. v3.2 adds the slate ramp: the product ground moves off sea-900 navy onto a neutral slate, which frees sea to mean measurement rather than background. Nothing was removed, so build-assets.py, build-plates.py and the Console Brand panel are unaffected.

ramps.name: Sea
ramps.role: The depth ramp. Grounds, structure, sequence, and every ordinal scale in a chart.
ramps.rule: sea-300 and lighter never carry text on paper.

ramps.name: Flame
ramps.role: The cue itself. The one thing that asks to be looked at.
ramps.rule: flame is never body text on paper (2.7:1) — use flame-600 or flame-700. One flame per screen region.

steps.note: graphic only — the mark, the cue dot

ramps.name: HUD
ramps.role: The product's own voice. Born in the glass; now also carries the interfaces that speak for it.
ramps.rule: hud green never touches a light ground. On dark it marks what the product itself says - the cue in the lens, a cue quoted back in Studio, and the HUD chrome of a nav. It is never a measurement: a passing check, a chart series or a bar is sea, because a wall of green ticks trains you to stop reading them.

ramps.name: Ink & paper
ramps.role: Editorial and marketing surfaces. The site is paper; the product is sea.

ramps.name: Slate
ramps.role: The product ground. Neutral, so sea can mean measurement instead of background.
ramps.rule: slate-800 is the ground and slate-100 the type on it. Never put slate-300 or lighter on slate-700 or lighter - it falls under 4.5:1.

faces.name: Instrument Sans
faces.role: Every functional job — UI, body, labels, headings in product.

faces.name: Instrument Serif
faces.role: Editorial only. ≥24px. Deliberately not loaded into the product UI.

faces.name: IBM Plex Mono
faces.role: Identifiers — SKUs, slugs, serials, commit hashes, anything you might read aloud or type back.

faces.name: Doto
faces.role: Cue Lens only. The dot-matrix face that matches the G2's monochrome grid.

mark.name: The Cue Bracket
mark.idea: An open C holding a single cue at its centre.
construction: grid 32 × 32 · arc centre (16,16) · radius 11 · round caps
gap 70° total, centred on the 3 o'clock axis
cue: solid circle at exact optical centre
clear space: one cue diameter (5.8 units) on all four sides
mark.minimum: 16px on screen, 6mm in print. Below that the opening closes and it reads as a filled ring.
rules: The cue is always flame. It never changes colour, on any ground.
The arc takes the ground: ink on light, paper on dark.
Never a low-chroma dot inside the C — it reads as a copyright glyph.
Never rotate. The opening is always on the right.
Always lowercase, always one word: cuesea.
Two-tone: cue in paper or ink, sea in sea-300 on dark or sea-500 on light. The split is what stops it slurring into "queasy" when read fast.

naming.name: Cue Studio
naming.what: The retailer-facing back office — floor performance, roster, analytics, administration.

naming.name: Cue Lens
naming.what: The in-glass surface on the Even Realities G2.
naming.note: The only thing an associate ever sees.

naming.name: Cue Console
naming.what: This internal console — cuesea staff only.

naming.name: Currents
naming.what: The CRM adapters. Shopify today, enterprise connectors later.
naming.note: Not yet renamed in code — still crm_provider.*

naming.name: Depth
naming.what: The AI service: grounded answers, recommendations, the cue grammar.
naming.note: Not yet renamed in code — still ai-service

principles: Say the thing. The lens has three lines and 60 characters — that discipline is the brand, not a constraint we apologise for.
Evidence before claim. "Bought the 32×30 in April" beats "likely interested in denim".
Never perform certainty we don't have. If stock is unknown, the glass says unknown.
Plain nouns over category jargon. An associate reads this while folding a sweater.

studio.label: Cue Studio / Cue Console
studio.note: Slate-grounded dense UI. Plex Mono for all identifiers, the depth ramp for every measurement, flame for the one thing per region that wants attention.

glass.label: The glass material
glass.note: Blur on exactly two surfaces - the topbar and the rail. Blur on a scrolling list is what janks a mid-range Android, so panels that scroll use --pane-solid.
